title: Inari puts the brakes on new aurora cabins and glass igloos
seoTitle: Inari curbs new aurora cabin building
description: Inari has tightened permits for aurora cabins and glass igloos. A 60-cabin resort west of Ivalo was rejected, and new capacity now waits for zoning.
dek: The municipal board rejected a 60-cabin project west of Ivalo in August 2025 and said building on that scale has to be settled in zoning.
heroAlt: A calm, undeveloped lake beside the road between Ivalo and Inari on a grey October day: still water in the foreground, a low forested ridge on the far shore and a bare birch on a rocky point to the right.
heroCaption: An unbuilt shore beside the road between Ivalo and Inari in October 2026. The rejected 60-cabin project was planned for a different site west of Ivalo village.

body.text: Inari has started to slow down the building of aurora cabins and glass igloos. For travellers it means new rooms will come slowly, and the best known places are worth booking earlier than before.

body.title: The Inari decision in brief
items: Rejected project: 60 aurora cabins west of Ivalo
Decision: the municipal board refused the permit on 4 August 2025
New zoning: west side of Saariselkä, announced on 25 March 2026
Plan areas: about 110 and about 23 hectares

body.text: According to Lapin Kansa the municipality has tightened the granting of permits, there are hardly any free plots left for newcomers, and the line has become considerably stricter over the past three years.

Vesa Pietikäinen, who has worked as the municipality's building inspector for a long time, says Inari has already had to use land policy to curb the enthusiasm for building aurora lodges. According to him people would like to build a tourism trap on every headland and in every hollow.

On 4 August 2025 the municipal board unanimously rejected a deviation permit sought by Wilderness Safaris Saariselkä Oy. The company wanted to build 60 aurora cabins and a restaurant of 600 square metres on an unbuilt plot west of Ivalo village, 2014 square metres of floor area in all. The site has neither a detailed plan nor a local master plan to guide building.

In its decision the board said the project would harm zoning and the other arrangement of land use, make it harder to reach nature conservation goals and lead to construction with significant effects.
Where tourism services are placed, and how many of them, has to be settled in an interactive zoning procedure in which the council holds the decision-making power.
The Lapland ELY Centre said in its statement that the values of the nationally valuable wind deposit and the esker area at Juurikangas would best be safeguarded by zoning.

The Sámi Museum Siida said the amount of new building was fairly large and its placement should be studied as part of a plan. The Hammastunturi reindeer herding co-operative said that a new tourism area large by Inari standards would form on the site and the peace of the area would be lost.

Inari's land policy programme, approved by the council on 8 December 2022, draws one of the lines. Outside the areas marked as tourism development zones in a local master plan or in the regional plan, the municipality accepts only traditional holiday home shore plans, not the more intensive shore plans that would allow tourism business.
Zoning on the west side of Saariselkä was announced on 25 March 2026 and is being prepared in two parts.

The Kaunispää plan amendment and extension covers about 110 hectares west of highway 4, where the aim is to zone the tourism service areas of the local master plan for functions that support accommodation at Saariselkä. The Kaunisniemi extension covers about 23 hectares and would allow the Northern Lights Village Saariselkä tourism area to grow.

For a traveller this means that the number of glass igloos and aurora cabins around Inari and Ivalo is not going to grow at the pace of the past few years. New rooms depend on plans that are still being prepared, so the best known places are worth booking further ahead than before for the darkest aurora weeks.
When rooms are scarce, the choice of base matters more than usual. You can find the places to stay in Inari village, Ivalo and the lake area on our Inari page.
